steps.say: CPPD is a chemistry problem of cartilage. Excess pyrophosphate made by ENPP1 leaves the cell through ANKH channels. Crystals are then the coating on fibrocartilage and hyaline surfaces. This figure contrasts CPPD crystals with gout crystals under polarized light.
steps.tx: Calcium pyrophosphate dihydrate (**CPPD**, the pseudogout crystal) deposition is driven by excess extracellular inorganic **pyrophosphate** (PPi, a phosphate dimer) generated by ectonucleotide pyrophosphatase **ENPP1** and exported from chondrocytes (cartilage cells) through the **ANKH** transporter. Surplus PPi meets calcium in cartilage and precipitates as rhomboid crystals. A metabolic or genetic boost to this pathway is the root of every CPPD phenotype below.

vis.alt: Polarised light microscopy comparing monosodium urate needles with calcium pyrophosphate rhomboids.
vis.caption: Rhomboid CPPD crystals are weakly positively birefringent while gout needles are strongly negative. Shape plus colour defines the crystal. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: Chondrocalcinosis on X-ray is the hallmark of CPPD. Thin calcific lines are the fill inside menisci, wrist cartilage, and pubic symphysis. The 2023 criteria accept bilateral imaging proof without fluid crystals. Every unexplained chronic arthritis requires a look at these three sites.
steps.tx: Calcified cartilage on X-ray is **chondrocalcinosis**, the signature of CPPD: delicate lines and dots lodged in knee menisci, the triangular wrist cartilage, the pubic symphysis, and glassy joint surfaces. Under 2023 ACR EULAR rules, disease is proven by **rhomboid** (diamond shaped) crystals under the microscope or by matching calcification on both sides. A calcified meniscus on a knee film indicates CPPD until proven otherwise.

vis.alt: Knee radiograph with arrows marking meniscal chondrocalcinosis and joint space narrowing.
vis.caption: Arrows mark meniscal calcification of chondrocalcinosis. Bilateral films satisfy classification without joint fluid. Image: Taokinesis, annotated by Mikael Haggstrom.

steps.say: Pseudogout is the acute face of CPPD with a hot knee, wrist, or shoulder. Above 50 percent of attacks are borne by the knees. Surgery, illness, or hyaluronan injections are the triggers of flares. Aspiration with steroid injection is the fastest relief.
steps.tx: A red hot joint exploding over hours is **pseudogout** (acute crystal synovitis): single or few joint arthritis hitting knees in above **50 percent**, plus wrists and shoulders. Bouts trail acute illness, operations like parathyroidectomy or joint replacement, or **hyaluronan** (viscosupplement) shots into the joint. Relief mirrors gout with joint aspiration plus glucocorticoid, oral **NSAID** therapy, or low dose colchicine, because suffering joints cannot wait for crystal proof.

vis.alt: Knee diagram with radiograph and polarized microscopy of chondrocalcinosis and rhomboid crystals.
vis.caption: Hot knee with meniscal calcification and rhomboid crystals defines pseudogout. Aspiration treats and proves at once. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: Chronic CPPD is the copy of rheumatoid arthritis joint by joint. Wrists, knuckles, and elbows are swollen symmetrically with cysts and stiffness. Negative RF and ACPA are the separators of the two diseases. Radiographic cysts with calcification confirm CPPD.
steps.tx: Chronic CPPD inflammatory arthritis (the **pseudo-rheumatoid** pattern) gives symmetric polyarthritis of wrists, MCP joints, and elbows with subchondral **cysts** (bone holes under cartilage) and morning stiffness, mimicking rheumatoid arthritis joint by joint. Negative rheumatoid factor and **ACPA** (anti citrullinated antibodies) separate the two, because true RA is seropositive in three quarters. Symmetric seronegative polyarthritis with cysts indicates CPPD, not RA.

points: RF and ACPA negative, cysts present
left.title: Chronic CPPD

points: RF or ACPA positive, no cysts

steps.say: Crowned dens syndrome is CPPD around the odontoid peg in the elderly. Severe neck pain with fever and stiffness is the mimic of meningitis. Non-contrast CT is where the retro-odontoid crown is seen. It is settled by steroids and colchicine without surgery.
steps.tx: In the elderly, crystals ringing the **odontoid** (the peg of the axis vertebra) build a **crowned dens**: cruciform and transverse ligament deposits with brutal neck pain, board like stiffness, fever, and rising markers. Plain CT without contrast discloses retro-odontoid **calcification** (a mineral crown hugging the peg). Fever plus stiff neck with a CT crown indicates CPPD, while lumbar puncture waits for true meningeal signs.

steps.say: Early or widespread CPPD indicates a metabolic driver. The top of the list is haemochromatosis, hyperparathyroidism, low magnesium, and low alkaline phosphatase. Patients below 50 with florid disease require the full metabolic panel. Treating the driver is the brake on new deposits.
steps.tx: Early onset or extensive CPPD indicates metabolic drivers: hereditary **haemochromatosis** (HFE iron overload blocking pyrophosphatase), primary **hyperparathyroidism** (excess parathyroid hormone), **hypomagnesemia** including Gitelman syndrome, and **hypophosphatasia** (ALPL mutations). Florid disease below 50 years requires iron studies, calcium with parathyroid hormone, magnesium, and alkaline phosphatase. A reversible driver is treated alongside the joints.

steps.say: Frequent pseudogout flares require daily low dose colchicine prophylaxis. Acute attacks are managed with aspiration, NSAID therapy, or colchicine. Doses are lower than gout regimens. Prophylaxis is reviewed yearly against flare counts.
steps.tx: Frequent recurrent pseudogout takes daily low dose **colchicine 0.5 mg to 0.6 mg** for flare prophylaxis, at doses lower than acute gout regimens. Each acute attack still takes aspiration with glucocorticoid injection, oral **NSAID** therapy, or short colchicine courses. Prophylaxis is reviewed yearly against flare counts and renal function, because colchicine accumulates in renal failure.

steps.say: Rhomboid positively birefringent crystals are the definition of the disease in fluid or tissue. Chondrocalcinosis is the definition on films. Pseudogout, pseudo-rheumatoid, and crowned dens are one chemistry in three clothes. Metabolic drivers are sought below 50.
steps.tx: Positively birefringent **rhomboid** crystals in fluid or tissue define CPPD, and bilateral **chondrocalcinosis** defines it on imaging under 2023 criteria. Pseudogout above **50 percent** in knees, symmetric seronegative polyarthritis with cysts, and crowned dens in the elderly are one chemistry in three clothes. Daily **colchicine 0.5 mg to 0.6 mg** holds recurrent disease while metabolic drivers are corrected.
